sections.body: Imaginary lines help us find places. LATITUDE lines run east–west and measure how far north or south you are. The EQUATOR is 0°.
LONGITUDE lines run north–south from pole to pole. The Prime Meridian (0°) passes through Greenwich, London.
Places near the equator are usually hot (tropical). Near the poles it's cold (polar). In between is temperate.
The world's longest river is either the Nile or the Amazon. Geographers still argue about how to measure them! The tallest mountain is Mount Everest (8,849 m).

options: The line of 0° latitude around the middle of the Earth
hints: It divides the Earth into north and south halves.
The Prime Meridian is 0° longitude. The line at 0° latitude is called the…?
quiz.explain: The Equator is 0° latitude, around the middle of the Earth.

quiz.q: Places near the Equator are usually…
hints: The Sun is strongest near the middle of the Earth.
Poles are cold because sunlight is weak there. What about the opposite place?
quiz.explain: Near the Equator, places are usually hot (tropical).
